picks.file: Messana, urbs est Siciliae maxima... - btv1b53178835x (1 of 2).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1 (colored copy, BnF)
picks.why: large richly colored copy; walled city behind the sickle-shaped harbor; name legend below cut

picks.file: Gezicht op Messina Messina (titel op object), BI-B-FM-090-72.jpg
picks.what: View across the harbor, colored engraving (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: color general view of the waterfront and harbor; Etna drawn smoking in the background as decoration; book page cut away

picks.file: Louis François Cassas's View of Messina Harbor with the Palazzata, designed by Simone Gullì in 1623.jpg
picks.what: The harbor and the Palazzata, drawing
picks.why: the famous curved harbor front before the 1783 earthquake destroyed it

picks.what: View over the city and harbor, engraving (Atlante illustrativo for Zuccagni-Orlandini’s Corografia dell’Italia)
picks.why: general view from the hill: rebuilt town, harbor arm and the Calabrian coast; second P3 view, 63 years after Cassas

picks.what: Panorama over the city and harbor, photograph (Hallwyl Museum, Stockholm)
picks.why: firmly dated view of the city 20 years before the 1908 earthquake; mount and caption cut

picks.what: The rebuilt city and the harbor, aerial photograph (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: whole city after post-earthquake rebuilding, with the sickle harbor; dark edge at right cut

picks.what: The city and the Christ the King shrine from the port, photograph
picks.why: sharp color view with the city’s best-known modern landmark above the town

gaps: P0: no candidates. P4 event (1908 earthquake ruins): no photograph of the ruins among the candidates; Beckmann’s 1909 painting (#27) is a figure scene, not a city view.
notes: P2 alternative: Willem Schellinks’s dated drawing of 30 November 1664 (#11), an eyewitness view from the east, pale gray ink. #17 Ducros 1789 watercolor of the ruined waterfront after the 1783 earthquake (event view, small file) left out since P3 already has two views. Sommer panoramas (#22, #23) dated only 1857–1914.
